title: The Goddess who holds Vishnu's sleep
hookLine: Vishnu sleeps on the cosmic waters, two demons rise to kill Brahma, and Brahma has to wake him
carry: shakti: even vishnu rests in her power
tomorrow: what is the fourth state, past deep sleep?

cards: Everything is water. One age of the world has ended, and the next hasn't begun. On that ocean, on the coils of a great serpent, Vishnu lies asleep.
From his navel rises a lotus, and on the lotus sits Brahma, the one who will make the next world. Then two demons, Madhu and Kaitabha, rise out of the dark and come for Brahma.
He looks down at the one person who could help him, and Vishnu doesn't stir. This sleep isn't ordinary. It has a name, and the name is today's word.

teach.h: BRAHMA PRAISES THE ONE WHO HOLDS THE SLEEP.
teach.b: The story opens the Devi Mahatmya, the Glory of the Goddess, a text set inside the Markandeya Purana. Brahma doesn't shake Vishnu. He doesn't shout.
He turns to the power that is holding Vishnu asleep, and he praises her. The text calls her Yoganidra. Yoga nidra: the sleep of yoga.
In this story she isn't a technique.
She is the Goddess herself, the great power behind creation, its keeping and its ending.
This is Shakti, power, and for Hindus who worship the Goddess as supreme, it's the deepest truth there is: the divine is power, and that power is a mother.
Brahma's hymn calls her by many names, among them the great night and the night of delusion, and also intelligence and understanding. Then he asks her to let Vishnu go. And she does.

teach.h: SHE LEAVES HIS EYES, HIS HEART. HE RISES.
teach.b: The text says she withdraws from his eyes, his mouth, his nose, his arms, his heart and his chest, and the Lord of the world rises to fight Madhu and Kaitabha.

teach.h: EVEN VISHNU RESTS IN HER POWER.
teach.b: That's why the text is the Glory of the Goddess, even though Vishnu does the fighting: without her, the preserver of the world can't open his eyes. And it's why, every Navaratri, temples and homes chant these chapters.
So yoga nidra, on this path, begins not as a technique but as a picture: a sleep that isn't absence, held by her.

how: Hindus who recite the Devi Mahatmya, especially during Navaratri, read Brahma's hymn to Yoganidra in its first chapter; some temples and households chant the whole text over several days.

s: in the Devi Mahatmya, yoga nidra is a relaxation technique
in the story, Yoganidra is the Goddess herself, the power holding Vishnu asleep.
Brahma wakes Vishnu by praising the one who holds his sleep
he sings a hymn to Yoganidra and asks her to let Vishnu go.
the text is called the Glory of the Goddess because she does all the fighting
Vishnu fights the demons, but only after Brahma praises her and she releases him: even his sleep and waking are her power.

games.q: you're Brahma, on a lotus over endless water. two demons are coming, and Vishnu won't wake. what do you do?
o: shake Vishnu and shout until he stirs.
praise the power that holds Vishnu asleep.
games.why: Brahma praises Yoganidra, the Goddess, and asks her to release Vishnu. She withdraws from his eyes, mouth, arms, heart and chest, and he rises.

practice: Lie down, or lean back in your chair, and let the body be heavy, as if resting on water.
Follow the story's waking slowly, in reverse: the chest rising and falling, the heart, the arms resting, the nose with the breath moving in it, the mouth soft, the eyes still behind the lids.
Don't try to sleep and don't try to stay alert; just rest and notice.

wordCard.voice: Yoga nidra. The sleep of yoga. In the Devi Mahatmya, it's the Goddess herself, holding Vishnu asleep on the waters.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: yoganidra, the sleep of yoga. In the Devi Mahatmya, a name of the Goddess.

carryVoice: Your line: Shakti, even Vishnu rests in her power. A sleep so full it has its own hymn. That's today, done.
